requirement: Habeas MUST bundle a skill for deriving initial requirements from an existing codebase. The skill MUST direct agents to read the code and tests, map every first-party test to at least one requirement or example, identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality or interactions to a requirement, and report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review.
rationale:
The single test, `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bootstrap_skill_is_bundled_and_directs_complete_inventories]`, covers every obligation in `requirements.cli.bootstrap_skill`. I did not read the skill text itself, only the test and its helpers.

- **Bundled skill.** `SKILLS` is asserted to contain `habeas-bootstrap-requirements`. `description(...)` is asserted to start with "Use when adopting Habeas in an existing codebase". The helpers read the skill through `skill_files`, which uses `include_str!` on the `assets/skills/...` files. So the assertions run against the bundled text.
- **Read the code and tests.** `assert_phrases` requires the phrases "Read the existing requirements, documentation, public entry points, implementation, and tests" and "Follow behavior through the code". It runs over `SKILL.md` plus its reference files, through `bundled_skill` and `assert_text`.
- **Map every first-party test to a requirement or example.** The test requires the phrases "every first-party runnable test or test case", "Record the behavior each test checks; fill in requirement names once they are installed", and "Every test must end up with a `{test}` reference to a requirement or example".
- **Identify and map every end-user-visible source unit.** The test requires these phrases:
  - "every function, method, struct, enum, and union, listed from the source to discover behavior no requirement states"
  - "public APIs, commands, handlers, UI actions, configuration, outputs, errors, and distinct observable branches"
  - "A tagged entry point doesn't mean every observable branch beneath it has a requirement"
  - "Give every inventoried test and each requirement's roots their references"
- **Report gaps and don't claim completeness without an independent review.** `assert_in_order` (via `assert_text_in_order`) requires this sequence: "recount both inventories from the source and tests without your lists", then the gap-report line format "- <item or behavior> (<file>:<line>): <reason>; <open question>", then "Claim 100% only when both inventories have no unmapped items", then "Don't silently exclude difficult cases".

The assertions are real content checks, not just execution. A skill that omitted any of these directives would fail them. The requirement states no further modes or boundaries, so I found no gaps.
